lesson.title: Writing a Description: Four to Five Sentences About Someone You Know
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: You have described yourself, a friend, and the whole class out loud. Today you write — a short, careful description of one person you actually know: a friend, a parent, a grandparent, a cousin. Four or five sentences, every adjective agreeing with that one person.

A strong description does more than list adjectives. Follow this order:

1. Who it is and how you know them: Mi abuela se llama Rosa. / Este es mi amigo Carlos.
2. Two or three personality adjectives, with a reason or example for at least one: Ella es muy trabajadora; cocina para toda la familia los domingos.
3. A contrast with pero: Es seria en el trabajo, pero muy graciosa en casa.
4. One thing you appreciate, or one thing you do together: Según toda la familia, es la persona más ordenada de la casa.

Then check every adjective: right ending for this person's gender, and singular, because it is one person.

Here is a finished five-sentence description:

Mi primo Daniel tiene doce años. Es muy atrevido: siempre prueba deportes nuevos como el skate y la escalada. También es gracioso y cuenta muchos chistes. Es un poco desordenado — su cuarto es un desastre. Pero según mi tía, Daniel es muy trabajador en la escuela.

Every adjective — atrevido, gracioso, desordenado, trabajador — is masculine singular, because Daniel is one boy. Swap in a female subject and all four would end in -a: atrevida, graciosa, desordenada, trabajadora.

You have drafted a real description with agreeing adjectives, a pero contrast, and según. Tomorrow you read it aloud while the class listens for the clues — including the -o and -a endings — and matches it to the right photo.

objectives: Write a 4-5 sentence description of a known person that names the relationship, two or three personality traits with an example, and a pero contrast
Keep every adjective in the description agreeing with the subject in gender and number
materialsNeeded: A photo or drawing of the person being described (for tomorrow)
Device for the build-the-sentence activity (optional — can be done on paper)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Recap the week's endings once more, including trabajador -> trabajadora.
2. Walk through the four-step description recipe.
3. Read the Daniel example aloud; have students find and check all four adjectives, then say the female version.
4. Students choose their person and draft on the worksheet — circulate and check agreement.
5. Complete the build-the-sentence activity as a warm-up or a break from drafting.
6. Students finish the 4-5 sentence draft and pick or make a photo/drawing for tomorrow.
7. Preview tomorrow's read-aloud and photo match.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide the four sentence starters (Mi ___ se llama..., Es..., pero..., Según...) and have them fill each one in
Ready for more: have them write two descriptions — one of a male and one of a female — so the -o/-a contrast is visible across the pair
If spelling the endings slows the writing down, let them draft freely first, then do one 'agreement pass' circling every adjective at the end
teacherGuide.answerKey: Descriptions vary. A complete response names the person and relationship, gives 2-3 personality adjectives (at least one with a reason/example), includes one pero contrast, and closes with an appreciation or shared activity. Every adjective must agree with the subject — masculine or feminine to match the person, singular because it is one person. Build-the-sentence: 1. Mi hermana es muy trabajadora. 2. Diego es serio pero gracioso. 3. Mis primos son atrevidos y graciosos. 4. Mi amiga es ordenada y trabajadora.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Delivers Day 4's scope-and-sequence design — a written 4-5 sentence description of a friend or family member — as the week's core WA-WL-2015.1.3 presentational-writing product, requiring sustained adjective agreement across a short connected paragraph rather than in isolated sentences, and reusing ser, pero, and según from earlier in the week.

worksheet.title: Writing a Description: Four to Five Sentences About Someone You Know

generationData.instructions: Plan and draft a 4-5 sentence description of one person you know.

rows.problem: Who will you describe, and what is your relationship? Write the first sentence (name + relationship).
List three personality adjectives for this person, spelled with the correct -o / -a / -s ending for them.
Write one 'pero' contrast sentence about this person.
Write your full 4-5 sentence description. Then circle every adjective and check its ending.
